newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares rise in healthy blue-chip demand.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares rise in healthy blue-chip demand.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange rose 0.13 percent on Tuesday in healthy foreign and local institutional demand for blue-chip cement, phosphate and potash firms, brokers said.
The market was buttressed by strong institutional demand for traditional market favourites including Arab Potash Co, Jordan Cement and Jordan Phospate Mines, some of it from international funds.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.21 points to 156.13 points in healthy trade worth 1,233,018 dinars.

Jordan Cement, the busiest stock which accounted for nearly half the day's volume, continues to attract strong local and foreign demand, brokers said. It rose 0.13 dinars to 3.93 dinars in high turnover worth 608,083 dinars.
Arab Potash was unchanged at 6.35 dinars in trade worth 93,974 dinars while Jordan Phosphates rose 0.10 dinars to 3.50 dinars in large trade worth 110,223 dinars.
National Portfolio rose a high 5.41 percent to 1.17 dinars in the second busiest trade of the day worth 128,465 dinars.
But Arab Bank, which is heavily weighted on the official index, fell again for a second day by 2.00 dinars to 257 dinars in minimal 31,040 dinar turnover.
Overall falling shares outnumbered gainers by 13 to 11 while 16 were unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.08 percent to 80.11 points, 3.94 percent down from the start of the year.
